name: luh-bethe-ansatz-data-for-the-open-d_3-2-spin-chain
notes:
Finite size Bethe ansatz data for the RG trajectories of low energy states of the D_3^(2) spin chain with open boundary conditions.

For details see: H. Frahm, S. Gehrmann, R. I. Nepomechie, Ana L. Retore (2025), "Quantum-group-invariant $D^{(2)}_{n+1}$ models: Bethe ansatz and finite-size spectrum": J. High Energy Phys. **2025**(12) (2025) 117 [arXiv:2509.00610].

###Boundary condition (0,0)
Symmetry is U_q(B_2) + Z2.

###Boundary condition (0,1)
Symmetry is U_q(B_1) x U_q(B_1) + Z2 + self-duality.  The partition function factorizes in two parts, each in the universality class of the antiferromagnetic Potts model with free ends.

###Boundary condition (1,0)
Symmetry is U_q(B_2) + Z2.

###Boundary condition (1,1)
Symmetry is U_q(B_1) x U_q(B_1) + Z2 + self-duality + "bonus symmetry". The analyzed low energy states fall into three categories:

* class A: the conformal weights can be decomposed into contributions of an antiferromagnetic Potts model with free ends and of the black hole CFT (continuous part and emerging discrete states)
* class B: one singular root - discrete states
* class C: two singular roots - discrete states with conformal weight linear in gamma (two Potts models as for BC (0,1))
title: Bethe ansatz data for the open $D_3^{(2)}$ spin chain

resources.description:
__Quantum-group-invariant $D^{(2)}_{n+1}$ models: Bethe ansatz and finite-size spectrum__, Holger Frahm, Sascha Gehrmann, Rafael I. Nepomechie, Ana L. Retore

Abstract: We consider the quantum integrable spin chain models associated with the Jimbo R-matrix based on the quantum affine algebra $D^{(2)}_{n+1}$, subject to quantum-group-invariant boundary conditions parameterized by two discrete variables p = 0, . . . , n and ε = 0, 1. We develop the analytical Bethe ansatz for the previously unexplored case ε = 1 with any n, and use it to investigate the effects of different boundary conditions on the finite-size spectrum of the quantum spin chain based on the rank-2 algebra $D^{(2)}_3$ . Previous work on this model with periodic boundary conditions has shown that it is critical for the range of anisotropy parameters 0 < γ < π/4, where its scaling limit is described by a non-compact CFT with continuous degrees of freedom related to two copies of the 2D black hole sigma model. The scaling limit of the model with quantum-group-invariant boundary conditions depends on the parameter ε: similarly as in the rank-1 $D^{(2)}_2$ chain, we find that the symmetry of the lattice model is spontaneously broken, and the spectrum of conformal weights has both discrete and continuous components, for ε = 1. For p = 1, the latter coincides with that of the $D^{(2)}_2$ chain, which should correspond to a non-compact brane related to one black hole CFT in the presence of boundaries. For ε = 0, the spectrum of conformal weights is purely discrete.

__Quantum-group-invariant $D^{(2)}_{n+1}$ models: Bethe ansatz and finite-size spectrum__, Holger Frahm, Sascha Gehrmann, Rafael I. Nepomechie, Ana L. Retore

Abstract: We consider the quantum integrable spin chain models associated with the Jimbo R-matrix based on the quantum affine algebra $D^{(2)}_{n+1}$, subject to quantum-group-invariant boundary conditions parameterized by two discrete variables p=0,...,n and epsilon = 0,1. We develop the analytical Bethe ansatz for the previously unexplored case epsilon = 1 with any n, and use it to investigate the effects of different boundary conditions on the finite-size spectrum of the quantum spin chain based on the rank-2 algebra $D^{(2)}_3$.
Previous work on this model with periodic boundary conditions has shown that it is critical for the range of anisotropy parameters 0<gamma<pi/4, where its scaling limit is described by a non-compact CFT with continuous degrees of freedom related to two copies of the 2D black hole sigma model.  The scaling limit of the model with quantum-group-invariant boundary conditions depends on the parameter epsilon: similarly as in the rank-1 $D^{(2)}_2$ chain, we find that the symmetry of the lattice model is spontaneously broken, and the spectrum of conformal weights has both discrete and continuous components, for epsilon=1. For p=1, the latter coincides with that of the $D^{(2)}_2$ chain, which should correspond to a non-compact brane related to one black hole CFT in the presence of boundaries. For epsilon=0, the spectrum of conformal weights is purely discrete.

 * the degeneracy of this state is g=18, twice as what is expected from the Uq(B1)xUq(B1) plus self-duality symmetries for this sector.
* this is a discrete state below a continuum.
resources.name: BC (1,1): class A-state #2 in sector (1,1)

 * the degeneracy of this state is g=18, twice as what is expected from the Uq(B1)xUq(B1) plus self-duality symmetries for this sector.

####pi/6<gamma<pi/4:

####gamma<pi/6:

resources.description:
Bethe roots for a state of the odd length D^{(2)}_3 spin chain with boundary conditions (epsilon=1,p=1) in the sector (h^l,h^r)=(1,2).

 * the degeneracy of this state is g=30, as expected for this sector.

####pi/6<gamma<pi/4:
* this is the lowest state from a continuum
* the subleading corrections to scaling are logarithmic

####gamma<pi/6:
* the state is a discrete state below a continuum of states
* the subleading corrections to scaling are power laws
* this is a discrete state below a continuum.
resources.name: BC (1,1): class A-state #1 in sector (1,2)

resources.description:
Bethe roots for a state of the even length D^{(2)}_3 spin chain with boundary conditions (epsilon=1,p=1) in the sector (h^l,h^r)=(1,1).

 * degeneracy of this state is g=18, twice what one expects for this sector
 * corrections to scaling are power laws

####0.14 pi<=gamma<pi/4:
 * the root configuration contains one singular root i.gamma on the first level in addition to the usual strings.

####gamma<=0.13 pi:
* one of the level-1 2-strings and then one of the level-2 ones are replaced by different configurations.
resources.name: BC (1,1): class B-state #1 in sector (1,1)
